bull_bear.body: Proposed final dividend of INR 4/share (total INR 6.50/share for FY26); cash reserves up 19% YoY to INR 2,637Cr; Board evaluating optimal use of cash (growth vs. returns), no buyback or M&A mentioned
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Client-specific operational issues recurring; AI productivity deflation delaying revenue recognition; slower-than-expected sales team ramp-up; competitive pressure from larger players in mid-market deals; geopolitical/tariff volatility; execution risk in new leadership integration
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident but cautious; acknowledges past underperformance; emphasizes 'bottom of the pit' turnaround; strong conviction in AI pivot and sales hires; avoids guidance due to volatility; tone is transformational, not defensive
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Cash build is the headline balance-sheet message: cash and cash equivalents of $304.1 M at end of Q1 FY27 from $278.1 M at end of Q4 FY26, described as up 9% QoQ and 26% YoY.
- The deck gives two different rupee figures for the same item: the CFO quote and Key Financial Highlights state cash and cash equivalents of Rs 28,786 M, while the 'Other operating highlights' bullet states Rs 28,768 M at the end of Q1 FY27 (from Rs 26,373 M at end of Q4 FY26). Both readings are reported here; they are not reconciled.
- Working capital discipline: Days Sales Outstanding - Billed improved to 55 days in Q1 FY27 from 62 in Q4 FY26 (58 in Q1 FY26), on the back of "strong collections".
- Cash flow for Q1 FY27: net cash generated from operating activities Rs 2,413 M / $25.4 M, net cash flow used in investing activities Rs (2,267) M / $(23.9) M, and net cash flow used in financing activities Rs (11) M / $(0.1) M.
- Hedge book (quarter ended Q1 FY26 / Q4 FY26 / Q1 FY27): USD Mn 73.0 / 72.0 / 43.0 at average rates of Rs 86.4 / 90.2 / 90.9; GBP Mn 7.7 / 4.8 / 3.3 at Rs 112.3 / 120.0 / 123.5; Euro Mn 6.7 / 5.5 / 3.5 at Rs 96.1 / 106.3 / 107.8.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: E&U: +1.8% QoQ growth; BFSI: stable spending but shift from traditional to AI work (P&C, payments, asset management); Life Sciences: -ve due to client-specific manufacturing/medtech ops issue (now behind); ERP: historically weak, now led by 25-year SAP veteran; Manufacturing: macro headwinds, but new sales hires focused here
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Self-described as a global technology company combining "industry proficiency with advanced digital capabilities" in Cloud, AI, Data and enterprise solutions, with "over 11,000 professionals"; it is part of the CKA Birla Group, led by Chairman Mrs. Amita Birla.
- The deck leans on third-party analyst positioning: 'Leader' in ISG Provider Lens Digital Engineering Services 2026; 'Product Challenger' in ISG Semiconductor Industry Services and Solutions 2026 and in ISG Microsoft AI and Cloud Ecosystem 2026; 'Horizon 1' in HFS Horizons Data Modernization and AI 2026.
- Further recognitions cited: 'Innovator' in Avasant High-Tech Industry Digital Services 2026 RadarView, 'Challenger' in Avasant Cybersecurity Services 2026 RadarView, 'Major Contender' in Everest's Oracle Cloud Applications Services and Oracle NetSuite Services PEAK Matrix 2025, and 'Major Player' in NelsonHall Salesforce Services NEAT 2026.
- Revenue is concentrating: client contribution to revenue (LTM) from Top 5 rose 37.8% (Q1 FY26) to 42.2% (Q4 FY26) to 43.4% (Q1 FY27), Top 10 from 52.5% to 55.2% to 56.2%, and Top 20 from 65.4% to 67.0% to 68.6%; the deck states contribution from Top 5, Top 10 and Top 20 customers increased QoQ.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Reinvestment intent] The CEO states the company will "continue to invest in our tech capabilities as well as in our sales force that should further strengthen our deals pipeline over the course of the year"; no capex amount, project or timeline is attached.
- [Macro] Management frames the quarter's 2.3% QoQ revenue growth as "stable performance in the face of a macro-environment that remains challenging".
- [Currency] Reported figures are sensitive to a moving rupee: average $/Rs rate of Rs 85.3 for Q1 FY26, Rs 92.8 for Q4 FY26 and Rs 95.0 for Q1 FY27 (period-end 85.76 / 94.83 / 94.66), which is why dollar revenue fell 0.1% QoQ while rupee revenue rose 2.3%; constant currency revenue is stated as up 0.3% QoQ and down 3.0% YoY.
- [Group] Part of the CKA Birla Group, an Indian multinational with over 35,000 employees and more than 50 manufacturing facilities, whose companies include Birlasoft, GMMCO, National Engineering Industries (NBC Bearings), BirlaNu (formerly HIL), Orient Electric, CK Birla Healthcare, Orient Paper, AVTEC and Neosym.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: 16.3% FY26 EBITDA margin driven by: rationalization of non-profitable accounts (200bps impact), operational efficiencies, currency tailwinds, and one-offs; future margin pressure expected from 30-40% sales team expansion, AI productivity front-ending, and leadership investments
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: no formal guidance, but management expects FY27 to be better than FY26; margin: steady-state target of 15%+ despite sales investments; order inflow: targeting substantially higher than FY26’s $750M TCV; capex/commissioning: minimal capex, investments focused on talent and AI platforms, not physical infrastructure
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: $208M TCV in Q4; $750M+ full-year FY26; net new TCV soft in Q4 due to client decision delays, not deal losses; 38% of TCV from net new business
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: AI-led managed services (Cogito platform); ERP modernization with SAP; expansion in U.S. Manufacturing & BFSI verticals; outcome-based contracts; new global partnerships (San Francisco-based leader); Lifesciences vertical leadership
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Despite 6.5% constant currency revenue decline in FY26 due to macro headwinds, client-specific issues in Life Sciences and deliberate exit from low-margin work, Birlasoft achieved 333bps EBITDA margin expansion to 16.3% and $208M Q4 order book — now pivoting to growth via 30-40% sales team expansion, new AI/ERP leaders, and AI-first delivery model, with revenue recovery expected in H2FY27 as pipeline converts.

risks.note: A substantial part of Birlasoft's revenue is derived from particular regions and customers; any adverse geopolitical or macroeconomic event in these areas could significantly impact performance, and lack of differentiation in service offerings combined with dependency on a few large clients poses a significant business risk.

Rapid innovation by hyperscalers, enterprise platform providers and data/analytics companies, combined with evolving Agentic AI capabilities, is increasing client demand for emerging-technology expertise and influencing customers' partner selection; the growth of Global Captive Centers (GCCs) in India and low-cost near-shore alternatives is also diverting client spend away from traditional IT services providers such as Birlasoft.

Birlasoft is pivoting from a people-intensive, staff-augmentation model to an AI-first, platform-enabled managed services model; insufficient internal readiness across skills, AI-infused offerings and evolving commercial constructs could cause revenue volatility, margin pressure from sub-optimal AI leverage, competitive vulnerability, and reputational impact.

Stringent and evolving US immigration and visa regulations (including H-1B and L-1 requirements) may restrict the Company's ability to deploy skilled resources onsite, potentially causing project delivery challenges, increased operational and compliance costs, reduced workforce mobility, and delayed project execution in a key geography.

Cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities and incidents can disrupt business, impact client service delivery, or result in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information; non-compliance with data privacy regimes such as GDPR, CCPA and India's DPDPA could result in significant regulatory penalties and reputational loss.

The IT services industry depends on the ability to attract, develop and retain skilled professionals aligned with fast-evolving technology and business strategy; rapid shifts in skill demand, particularly in niche, high-demand AI areas, create risk if the Company cannot secure or retain such talent.
risks.risk: Talent resourcing, retention and upskilling risk

risks.note: Birlasoft faces operational, contractual and financial risks in executing customer projects, including the inability to meet contractual obligations and service level agreements, which could impact reputation, revenue, profitability and potentially lead to legal disputes.

Birlasoft's Climate Risk Assessment has identified physical risks such as extreme heat and water scarcity at certain locations, and transition risks from changing regulations, disclosure requirements and stakeholder expectations, which if not addressed proactively could impact operational continuity, client confidence, sustainability ratings and financial performance.
